category_title: Secondary PRU students with low self-worth and mainstream avoidance
scenario_title: Navigating perceived pressure and behavioral expectations in mainstream versus alternative provision
minimal_context: The tutor is asking the student to complete a GCSE practice paper in a mainstream classroom setting.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: We need to complete this GCSE practice paper today. It is important to finish this so you can prepare for your exams.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I know you need GCSEs to get to go to a good college to get a career. But the school wanting that good reputation so choosing the normal kids... but then the people that are below that standard are like the outcasts...

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's just focus on the questions in front of you right now.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: If you can get through mainstream then [sighs] congratulations basically... You either deal with it or you don't... I had to back away, it was too much.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You need to keep working. I heard about the incident in the hallway earlier, and you need to show you can behave and finish this assignment.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: She pushed me over so I punched her in the face! You're always blaming me. The school's corrupt... They got me excluded... The internal exclusion happened... I can't avoid it...

task.content: Participating in the learning curriculum under perceived pressure and high expectations
task.learning_goal: To get GCSEs to get to go to a good college to get a career

context.environment: Mainstream education environment with perceived pressure, or alternative provision (PRU) settings with increased space and 'calmness'
context.materials: Active and personalised nature of the learning curriculum, organisational structure (reward systems)
context.social_setting: Interactions where the student feels unsupported and disliked by teachers, or settings with increased adult support such as a youth worker

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: Being annoyed or targeted by peers, feeling unsupported and disliked by teachers or being unfairly blamed
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Anger and 'revenge style' behaviour, such as physical retaliation
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Strong but rigid belief for the need for equality, lack of flexibility in thinking, feeling 'targeted'
related_quotes: She pushed me over so I punched her in the face.

behavior_patterns.condition: Facing the perceived pressure and high expectations of the mainstream school environment
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Backing away, withdrawing from the situation, and generalising displeasure to mainstream education as a whole
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Feelings of inadequacy and perceived failure in not fitting in with 'convention', feeling like 'outcasts'
related_quotes: I had to back away, it was too much.
The school wanting that good reputation so choosing the normal kids. . .but then the people that are below that standard are like the outcasts. . .

behavior_patterns.condition: When discussing behavioural difficulties or facing disciplinary action like internal exclusion
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Attributing behavioural difficulties to external factors, showing passivity in how they accept future circumstances
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Sense of learned helplessness in capacity to change, sense of unfairness, reflecting the role of victim
related_quotes: The internal exclusion happened. . .I can ’t avoid it. . .
